original_question: Let f : PN → PN be a morphism of degree d defined over Q. (a) For which n ≥ 1 is it true that f has a point of exact period n in PN (Q) if and only if f has a point of exact period n in PN (R) and in PN (Qp ) for all primes p?
target_in_paper: Question 22.2(a) in Section 22 (Local-Global Questions in Dynamics), with Theorem 22.1 as the immediately preceding motivating result.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper. It has the correct object (a morphism f:P^N -> P^N defined over Q), the correct dynamical property (existence of a point of exact period n), the correct local fields (R and Q_p for all primes p), and the correct local-global equivalence. In substance, it is essentially Question 22.2(a).
missing_details: The quantifier over f should be made explicit: the paper is asking for which integers n >= 1 the stated equivalence holds for every morphism f:P^N -> P^N of the given degree d over Q.
The meaning of exact period n should be spelled out: there should exist P in P^N(Q) with f^n(P)=P and f^i(P) != P for every 1 <= i < n.

To be fully stand-alone, morphism of degree d over Q should be unpacked as an everywhere-defined endomorphism of projective space given in homogeneous coordinates by forms of common degree d with rational coefficients.
The ambient parameters are fixed N and d; n is the variable being classified.
A paper-faithful restatement should avoid inserting an extra restriction d >= 2, since Question 22.2(a) itself does not explicitly impose it.
The paper notes that the question is stated over Q only for simplicity and is easily generalized to number fields; that contextual remark is implicit in the draft.
refined_question: Fix N >= 1 and a degree d. For which integers n >= 1 does the following local-global principle hold for every morphism f:P^N -> P^N defined over Q, i.e. every everywhere-defined endomorphism of projective N-space given by homogeneous forms of common degree d with rational coefficients: f has a Q-rational point of exact period n (equivalently, there exists P in P^N(Q) such that f^n(P)=P and f^i(P) != P for all 1 <= i < n) if and only if f has a point of exact period n in P^N(R) and in P^N(Q_p) for every prime p?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 22 rather than any earlier part of the survey. The exact matching item is Question 22.2(a), whose wording is almost identical to your draft. The nearby context matters: the authors first motivate the local-global theme and state Theorem 22.1 for quadratic polynomials on P^1, then immediately pose Question 22.2(a). To make the question fully self-contained, one must import earlier notation from Definition 2.1 (exact period) and Section 3 (P^N(K), morphisms of P^N, and degree). The paper also explicitly remarks just before Question 22.2 that the formulation over Q is for convenience and can be generalized to number fields. Because your draft only asks about the equivalence itself, the closest paper-faithful target is part (a) alone, not part (b) or the broader follow-up about preperiodic points of type (m,n).
